title: The Creator Campaign HQ in Claude
subtitle: Seven prompts to shortlist, brief, check and report on creators from one Claude Project.
hook: Run your whole creator campaign from one Claude Project
caption:
Run your whole creator campaign from one Claude Project 👇

The full guide covers the setup step by step, with every prompt.

What I'd run:

1/ Set up the HQ
Brief, brand rules and past results go in as files.
Every chat starts already knowing the campaign.

2/ Shortlist from the brief
Claude ranks your exported list and quotes the evidence.
You choose on fit, not follower count.

3/ Vet the comments
Public comments become evidence, concerns and questions.
Never looks, never sensitive traits. Only the work.

4/ Draft outreach
It writes around one real line you wrote per creator.
You read every message and send it yourself.

5/ Write the one-page brief
Built from your master brief, with gaps marked.
Creators get one screen they will actually read.

6/ Check drafts and labels
Each draft is checked against the brief and your ad-label rules.
You catch the missing must-say before it goes live.

7/ Weekly report
Export your numbers and get a one-page report with the maths shown.
Check two figures by hand, then send.

I've worked on 850+ creator deals on the brand side.
In creator campaigns, most problems start with a vague brief.
So the brief is the first file in the HQ.

Setup takes about an hour, and a free Claude account is enough to start.

Comment CREATOR and I'll send you the full guide.

pages.kicker: THE MINI GUIDE · NO FLUFF, JUST STEPS
pages.title: Your creator campaign HQ in Claude
pages.sub: Seven steps, seven prompts, one Project.

pages.title: Put the brief at the centre
pages.body: Create one Project per campaign. Upload five short files: brief, brand rules, past results, creator list, ad-label rules. Add standing instructions so every chat starts informed.
pages.prompt: You are the HQ assistant for [campaign]. Use only the Project files and what I paste. If something is missing, say "not in the files". Never infer sensitive traits or rate looks. Quote your evidence. Draft only: I decide and I send.

pages.title: Rank creators on fit, not followers
pages.body: Export your longlist as a CSV with a notes column. Claude scores each creator against the brief and quotes the row it used. You check two or three figures yourself.
pages.prompt: Using file 01 and file 04, shortlist the best [8] creators. Score 1 to 5 on brief fit, content, engagement health, cost and brand safety. Table: Creator | Score | Why (quote the row) | Risk | Question to ask. Say "not in the files" for missing data.

pages.title: Turn a hunch into questions
pages.body: Paste five captions and 20 to 30 public comments. Claude lists evidence, concerns and questions to ask. Flags are questions, not verdicts, and it never guesses sensitive traits.
pages.prompt: Vet [Creator A] using the pasted captions and comments plus files 01 and 02. Check fit, generic versus specific comments, and competing sponsors. Never infer sensitive traits or comment on appearance. Answer: Evidence, Concerns with quotes, Questions to ask.

ui.title: Vetting chat (example)
rows: You: Vet Creator A for this campaign
Claude: Evidence: comments ask about the product
Claude: Concern: many comments are emoji only
Claude: Ask: can you share audience insights?

pages.title: One real line makes it personal
pages.body: Write one line per creator about a post you liked. Claude drafts a short message around it. You read every message and send it from your own account.
pages.prompt: Draft a first message for each creator below, using file 01 and my note. Under 90 words. Open with my note, say it is a paid collaboration, make one clear ask, offer the one-page brief. No flattery I did not supply. Table: Creator | Subject | Message.

ui.title: Email draft (example)
rows: Hi Creator A, your video on [topic] ...
May I send a one-page brief?

pages.title: Give creators one screen to read
pages.body: Claude builds the brief from your master file: the one thing, must-say, must-not-say, dates and label line. Gaps are marked [TO CONFIRM]. Payment and rights stay in the contract.
pages.prompt: Turn files 01 and 02 into a creator brief under 250 words: the one thing, audience, must-say, must-not-say, deliverables and dates, measurement, ad label line, approvals. Leave out payment and rights. Mark gaps as [TO CONFIRM].

pages.title: Check every draft before it posts
pages.body: Claude checks each draft against the brief and your label rules, quotes the line, and marks Pass, Fix or Unclear. Then you check the live post on your phone.
pages.prompt: Check the draft below against files 01, 02 and 05. Table: Check | Pass, Fix or Unclear | Quote | Fix. Cover the one thing, must-say lines, claims, label wording and position, format. If you cannot see it, mark Unclear, never Pass.

pages.title: Report from numbers you exported
pages.body: Export the figures into one CSV each week. Claude drafts a one-page report with formulas shown and gaps flagged. Check two numbers by hand, then save it back into the Project.
pages.prompt: Write this week's report from the attached CSV: headline sentence, table by creator, what worked, what did not, next action per creator (keep, adjust, stop). Use only CSV numbers, show every formula, flag mixed definitions, mark gaps "not in the data".
